name: Ready to Work (Boys & Girls Clubs of Boston)
what_you_do: Teen members get workshops to get ready for jobs. Topics are coding, digital literacy, communication and teamwork. They get help with resumes. They get career coaching. They also get hands-on internships. Fields include healthcare, culinary arts and finance.
who_can_apply: Teen members of Boys & Girls Clubs of Boston, which serves ages 6 to 18 at clubs in Boston and Chelsea. The page gives no age rule for the workforce program itself.
pay_detail: The page says the internships are paid but gives no pay rate. The Clubs report about 500 teen jobs and internships a year.
deadline_text: No dates are posted on the page.
how_to_apply: The page does not explain how teens are placed. Find your nearest Club on the Find Your Club page and ask about the Ready to Work program and the Club's Employment Specialist. General contact page: bgcb.org/contact-us.
notes: Confirm first: ages, hours and how to apply are not on the page. Under Massachusetts law (M.G.L. c.149 s.86) a child employed needs a work permit from the superintendent of schools, so ask the Club how permits are handled. The Clubs' home page said membership fees were waived for the 2025 to 2026 school year; ask about this year's fee. Teen centers: Mildred C. Hailey Teen Center (Jamaica Plain) and Josh Kraft Mattapan Teen Center. See permit.html?state=ma for the exact permit and steps.
